=== CONSENSUS FINDINGS ===
- scripts/orchestrate_poll_process.sh:lines 233-236 and 20686-20690 | severity=major | confidence=[4]
  flagged_by: [deepseek_deepseek-v4-pro, minimax_minimax-m3, moonshotai_kimi-k3, qwen_qwen3_7-plus, x-ai_grok-4_6]
  PROBLEM: When both truncation paths fail, `_judge_truncate_pr_diff_file` returns success without modifying the file, so the caller embeds the full untruncated diff, deducts only the configured allowance, and falsely logs successful truncation.
  WHY: This can reintroduce oversized judge prompts and opaque `Input exceeds the maximum length` failures on affected runners.
- scripts/orchestrate_poll_process.sh:lines 20857-20862 and line 20875 onward | severity=major | confidence=[4]
  flagged_by: [deepseek_deepseek-v4-pro, minimax_minimax-m3, qwen_qwen3_7-plus, x-ai_grok-4_6]
  PROBLEM: An already-over-cap prompt is still submitted through both identical judge attempts instead of failing before the retry loop.
  WHY: The retry attempts cannot change the unchanged oversized prompt and waste codex invocations and wall time before the existing failure telemetry; qwen_qwen3_7-plus rated this as NIT, but the highest severity is used.
- scripts/orchestrate_poll_process.sh:20857-20862 | severity=major | confidence=[3]
  flagged_by: [deepseek_deepseek-v4-pro, minimax_minimax-m3]
  PROBLEM: `wc -c` measures bytes while the codex limit is expressed in characters, causing the 950,000 warning threshold to fire early for multibyte UTF-8 prompts.
  WHY: The warning can become routine and lose diagnostic value; moonshotai_kimi-k3 rejected this finding and rated the existing byte-based comparison as a safe conservative check, so the highest reported severity is used with that disagreement noted.
- README.md:JUDGE_PR_DIFFS_TOTAL_MAX_BYTES row, description text: "The poller logs Judge prompt size: N bytes before every judge exec" | severity=major | confidence=[4]
  flagged_by: [deepseek_deepseek-v4-pro, minimax_minimax-m3, moonshotai_kimi-k3]
  PROBLEM: The README says prompt size is logged before every judge exec, but the implementation logs it once per judge phase before the first exec.
  WHY: The documentation misrepresents observable retry logging and can mislead incident response; deepseek_deepseek-v4-pro and moonshotai_kimi-k3 rated this NIT, but the highest severity is used.

=== END CONSENSUS FINDINGS ===

=== FINDINGS FROM deepseek_deepseek-v4-pro ===
- scripts/orchestrate_poll_process.sh:lines 206-236, specifically the terminal else branch (233-235) and the call site at lines 20686-20690 | severity=major | confidence=[4]
  PROBLEM: When both python3 and head -c fail, the helper removes the temp file but leaves `_pr_diff_capped_tmp` untruncated while returning 0, so the caller embeds the full payload and logs successful truncation.
  WHY: The prompt can exceed codex's 1 MB stdin cap despite misleading truncation logs.
- scripts/orchestrate_poll_process.sh:line 20687, the unconditional echo "Judge context: PR #${PR_NUM} (issue #${inum}) diff truncated from ${_pr_diff_bytes} to ${_pr_diff_allowance} bytes ..." | severity=major | confidence=[4]
  PROBLEM: The truncation log line is emitted regardless of whether the helper succeeded.
  WHY: The log reports a byte count that may not match the actual file content and hides the failure.
- scripts/orchestrate_poll_process.sh:lines 20859-20862, JUDGE_PROMPT_BYTES measurement and warning before the attempt loop | severity=major | confidence=[3]
  PROBLEM: The prompt size is warned about but both judge attempts still run against the same oversized file.
  WHY: An over-cap prompt fails identically on every attempt and wastes a full codex-cli invocation per attempt.
- scripts/orchestrate_poll_process.sh:lines 20857-20858, JUDGE_PROMPT_BYTES measured with wc -c | severity=nit | confidence=[2]
  PROBLEM: `wc -c` counts bytes while the codex cap is measured in characters.
  WHY: The warning can fire for prompts that are under the character limit, reducing the warning's usefulness.
- README.md:JUDGE_PR_DIFFS_TOTAL_MAX_BYTES row, description text: "The poller logs Judge prompt size: N bytes before every judge exec" | severity=nit | confidence=[2]
  PROBLEM: The README says the size is logged before every judge exec although it is logged once per judge phase.
  WHY: The documentation gives operators an incorrect expectation during retries.
=== END FINDINGS FROM deepseek_deepseek-v4-pro ===

=== FINDINGS FROM minimax_minimax-m3 ===

  PROBLEM: The helper returns 0 when both truncation paths fail, leaving the oversized content in place while the caller embeds it, deducts only the allowance, and logs successful truncation.
  WHY: The README claim that the byte cap keeps the prompt under codex's 1 MB stdin cap is silently broken on this failure path.
- scripts/orchestrate_poll_process.sh:judge prompt size check (≈ lines 20857-20862) and the judge exec loop (≈ line 20875) | severity=major | confidence=[4]
  PROBLEM: An over-cap prompt still enters both identical judge attempts before the existing judge-failed path emits its alert.
  WHY: The retry loop burns codex call budget and several minutes of wall time without any chance of recovery.
- scripts/orchestrate_poll_process.sh:JUDGE_PROMPT_BYTES measurement (≈ line 20857) compared with the 950000-byte warning threshold | severity=major | confidence=[3]
  PROBLEM: `wc -c` counts bytes while codex enforces a character cap, so multibyte prompts can trigger the warning while remaining acceptable.
  WHY: Routine false-positive warnings degrade the diagnostic value of the threshold.
- README.md:JUDGE_PR_DIFFS_TOTAL_MAX_BYTES row in the orchestrate_poll variable table (≈ line 1187) | severity=major | confidence=[4]
  PROBLEM: README claims "The poller logs `Judge prompt size: N bytes` before every judge exec", but the implementation logs once before the first codex exec.
  WHY: The operator-facing documentation contradicts retry behavior.
- README.md:JUDGE_PR_DIFFS_TOTAL_MAX_BYTES row in the orchestrate_poll variable table (≈ line 1187) | severity=nit | confidence=[4]
  PROBLEM: The documentation's "before every judge exec" claim does not match the single size log emitted per tick.
  WHY: Operators may infer the implementation is wrong or has regressed when only one line appears.
